text: When working with APIs, you typically send HTTP requests to a server and receive responses in JSON format. First, you need authentication—often an API key—to access the service. Then, you make requests like GET or POST to retrieve or send data. However, APIs usually have rate limits, so you cannot make too many requests in a short time. If you exceed the limit, you might get an error. Good error handling is important: always check the response status code and handle problems like network failures or invalid data. Understanding these basics will help you integrate APIs smoothly into your applications.
